 CHIEF JUSTICE ROBERTS:  We'll hear
 argument first this term in Case 25-170, Suncor
Energy versus County Commissioners of Boulder
 County.
 Mr. Shanmugam.
 ORAL ARGUMENT OF KANNON K. SHANMUGAM
 ON BEHALF OF THE PETITIONERS
 MR. SHANMUGAM:  Thank you, Mr. Chief
Justice, and may it please the Court:
 This case involves an unprecedented
effort to use state law to regulate global
 conduct.  Boulder is suing Petitioners under
Colorado law on the theory that their global
 conduct increased the global use of fossil
fuels, which led to an increase in global
 greenhouse-gas emissions, which contributed to
global climate change, which resulted in global
 harms.
 Our constitutional system does not
permit state law to be used in that manner.
 The Constitution bars the application of state
 law to certain inherently federal areas.  When
 the states entered the Union, the plan of the

Convention required them to surrender certain
preexisting powers in order to ensure each
 state's equal sovereignty.
 Because of the ambient nature of air
and water and the conflicting rights of states,
 this Court has held for over a century that
federal law governs interstate pollution
 claims.  That principle applies with even
greater force to claims involving global
 climate change.
 In addition, the Constitution's
 prohibition on extraterritorial regulation
precludes a state from extending its law beyond
 its borders to regulate global conduct with
global effects. A state does not have the
 power to regulate out-of-state conduct based
solely on attenuated effects on the state.
 What is more, the use of state law to
 regulate global climate change would
 substantially interfere with the nation's
foreign policy. And far from authorizing the
 application of state law, the Clean Air Act
independently preempts any effort by one state
to impose its law on emissions originating in
 others.

that because this case did not involve a formal
writ proceeding directed at the lower court,
that it falls outside the scope of Atlantic

 this Court attached no weight to the form of

court to respond to its order to show cause and

made that move toward a more informal label for
